bullets.title: Welcome to GNPS Program 8
bullets.text: Compassionate Mental Health Care Program Outline Welcome to GNPS Level 2 - International Qualified Nurse. International mental health practice expects nurses to combine therapeutic engagement with structured assessment, evidence-based intervention, legal awareness, cultural safety and multidisciplinary collaboration. This level bridges national nursing preparation with international expectations. …

bullets.title: Comprehensive Assessment, Formulation and Care Planning
bullets.text: International mental health practice expects nurses to integrate mental state findings, history, physical health, trauma, substance use, culture and current risk. Assessment informs a shared formulation and individualised plan rather than a diagnosis alone.

bullets.title: Managing Suicide, Self-Harm and Acute Behavioural Disturbance
bullets.text: High-risk mental health presentations require calm, structured and legally informed care. Nurses should respond to the immediate risk while preserving dignity, therapeutic engagement and future recovery.

bullets.title: Psychopharmacology, Physical Health and Co-occurring Conditions
bullets.text: People using mental health services may experience medication effects, physical illness and substance-related problems that influence mental state and risk. International nurses are expected to monitor the whole person.

bullets.title: Legal, Ethical and Culturally Safe International Practice
bullets.text: Mental health law and policy differ across jurisdictions, but core principles include dignity, autonomy, confidentiality, proportionality and least restrictive care. International nurses must learn the local legal framework before independent practice.
